correctness.rationale: For \(m=2\), the zero-sum relation is an antipodal pair and the local statement is immediate. For \(m\ge3\), each normalized squared modulus is at most \((m-1)/m\). A direct polygon/Cauchy argument proves the exact fourth-moment bound \(B=(m^2-3m+3)/(m(m-1))\). For \(q=p/2>2\), the quadratic Hermite interpolant to \(t^q\) with a double node at \(1/(m(m-1))\) and a node at \((m-1)/m\) majorizes \(t^q\) on the full interval because its Hermite error has the sign of \((t-r)^2(t-M)\), and its quadratic coefficient is positive. Summing the majorant and inserting the fourth-moment bound gives the claimed sharp zero-sum constant. Strict equality forces the one-versus-\((m-1)\) modulus profile and collinear phases. Coset zero-mean decomposition then gives the finite-group constant; strict convexity forces a single active coset, and Fourier inversion gives exactly the stated flat coefficient extremizers. The bundled verifier replays 224224 majorant samples, 16560 random zero-sum regressions, 1248 fourth/sixth-moment algebra checks, and 216 explicit cyclic extremizer checks. These computations corroborate rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: Complements of dual subgroups are a natural structured family of finite \(\Lambda(p)\) sets. Extending exact sharp constants from isolated polynomial moments to every real \(p>4\) is a continuum norm theorem, and the proof identifies the reusable finite-dimensional mechanism: a sharp zero-sum-hyperplane \(\ell^2\to\ell^p\) inequality with complete equality class. The group result is group-structure independent and classifies all extremizers, so it is not an arbitrary slice, a numerical recomputation, or a routine parameter increment.
